question: When a crowd has to flee a bombing or a fire, what do most people in it do?
answer: Help each other. Interviewing survivors of the 2005 London bombings, Drury, Cocking and Reicher found selfish stampeding was rare; people felt a common fate and helped strangers. The bigger danger is delay, not frenzy. Deadly crushes come from density, when too many bodies fill too little space, not from panic.
move: Expect strangers in trouble to cooperate, and plan for slowness rather than frenzy.
ask: In an emergency, would I waste time expecting chaos, or move early and help the people around me?
reference: Drury, Cocking & Reicher, The nature of collective resilience: survivor reactions to the 2005 London bombings, International Journal of Mass Emergencies and Disasters, 2009
